bet.text: Replace the single-stream turret with a drum shooter, so the robot scores more fuel per second, runs more cycles and negates fuel starvation.

demand.text: Throughput into the hub. After district events the team judged that its turret could not stay competitive with higher scoring robots and that opponents limited it by starving it of fuel. A drum lets it score larger loads, run more cycles, shuttle fuel during the other alliance's shift and starve opponents itself.

auto.text: A custom path follower blends go-to-point with timing, so a robot stuck on fuel continues to its next path; the team says it can miss its first grab and still score around 40 to 50. A tool overlays partner autos to find collisions.
One recorded alliance plan has it go to the middle twice.

cycle.text: The intake takes four fuel at once into the hopper; a four-wide indexer speeds them up toward the feeder and the drum shoots them. During the other alliance's active shift it shuttles fuel to its own side.

endgame.text: The packet describes two pivoting hooks, linked to a static shaft by surgical tubing and stowed by a Dyneema spool, meant to climb from several tower positions and hold the robot after the match.

fallback.text: With the hood rollers out of the way it can shoot toward the other side of the robot, a last resort against defense and shot blockers, then at about 50% accuracy.
The team ran out of time and did not find it consistent enough to use in a match.

gave_up.text: With the drum as its only flywheel, the team relies on software tuning to handle velocity spikes.
A post says 1323 and 4065 used shot blockers against 6800 and 254 in Einstein playoff match 8, and calls blocking the counter to the dominant scoring archetype.
A reply disputes that this was the first counter: in the Archimedes finals one alliance kept rotating drum shooters.

changed.text: It began with a turret and wanted more throughput after its first competition.
Its packet dates the drum after district events.
Archetypes were reconsidered after week 1 and development began in week 3.
A linear intake that shredded teeth and took hopper space became a slapdown; four rollers became one.
In Einstein match 3 hard driving and too aggressive supply limits blew the main breaker; lower limits fixed it.

outcome.text: 62-10-0 in official play; won the Curie division; captain of the Curie alliance on Einstein; ranked 12 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 313.95, Curie).

solves.text: Survive high-speed collisions and drive over the bump quickly with a low center of gravity

facts.text: Square frame side, sized for fuel capacity
WCP Swerve X2c modules and 2 x 2 in chassis rails
For intake efficiency and to keep fuel from being compressed under the chassis, bumpers were lowered to

solves.text: Take in a mass of fuel quickly instead of controlling the path of each piece

facts.text: Width, for four fuel at once
One powered 2 in roller and one static 1 in aluminum tube; two Kraken X60s at 1.23:1
Deploys on a single pivot from one low-mounted Kraken X60 through two ThriftyBot cycloidal gearboxes, 69:1, under the feeder rollers
A custom spline shaft connects the two cycloidals
An earlier crash bar bent inward and stalled the rollers; a 1 in round tube, moved above the rollers and with extra bracing on the motor plates, replaced the 2 x 1 tube
A hard stop meets the output arm at both ends of travel; the gearboxes are usually aligned resting on the down stop
The belt reduction to the jackshaft never skipped, as far as the team knows, at any of the ratios it ran

cost.text: By September, after more than 55 matches and over three times that in practice, the cycloidals had slightly more backlash; still working, they were replaced on the competition robot that off-season
One 1/2 to 3/8 in hex adapter in the deploy fatigued and added backlash

functions.name: Hopper

solves.text: Carry more fuel while still passing under the trench when the bump is defended
Keep fuel from falling straight from the hub into the robot, which could draw penalties

functions.type: expanding hopper with top net and bumper-mounted panels

facts.text: Volume unextended
Volume extended
The net adds about 15 fuel, for about 75 in all
Walls are 1/8 in, tied to the shooter and intake

solves.text: Move four fuel at once from intake to feeder while staying low for hopper room

facts.text: Two Kraken X44s at 2.5:1; a mix of 2 in and 1.25 in rollers speeds fuel up gradually
Faster on the shooter side and slower on the intake side, so there are no choke points
Held by four screws, two on each side, which lets the electronics sit on top of the belly pan for service

functions.name: Feeder and Shooter

solves.text: A single-stream turret did not score enough fuel per second

functions.type: four-wide drum shooter with adjustable hood

facts.text: The drum is a single aluminum tube, wrapped in grip tape, of diameter
Three Kraken X60s at 3:2 drive the shooter; two Kraken X60s at 20:9 drive the feeder; feeder rollers are 2 in
One Kraken X44 at 1580:21 moves the hood through
Spin-up time about
The team says it scores up to about three times the fuel per second of the turret robot
Spacers pull the shooter plates inward and the pulleys sit close to the robot edge, to fit a shooter four fuel wide in a square chassis
A team post gives the hood ratio as 790:11, about 71.8:1, against the packet's 1580:21, and says anything from 60:1 to 80:1 should work
Feeder rollers get less compression than the drum, to reduce current draw
Compression between drum and hood rollers is a compromise between efficiency and range
Most printed gears are carbon-fiber nylon (PA612-CF15); milled versions were made but the team stayed with nylon, and the abrasive fiber made little difference in practice

cost.text: The inconsistent reverse shot comes mainly from polycarbonate feeder rollers, which vary compression and exit angle; the team planned an aluminum top roller
A herringbone gearset tried on the hood's reverser rollers melted and fatigued after about 5 min of running; the team advises straight-cut 10 DP there

functions.type: two pivoting hooks with surgical tubing and spool

facts.text: Hooks are 3/8 in aluminum plates; surgical tubing links them to a static shaft and a spool winds Dyneema to stow them
Kraken X44 through a 23:1 cycloidal and two gears, total reduction 74.1:1

functions.name: Electrical panel

solves.text: Protect electronics from bump damage and from fuel hitting the bottom of the robot

functions.type: single belly pan, electronics on top

facts.text: Most components sit on a single belly pan, with protective plates for crossing the bump
A battery swap means turning the robot over, removing four screws from a bottom plate and cutting a zip tie that keeps the lead from falling out on the bump

functions.name: Valkyrie software library

solves.text: Keep an auto going after the robot gets stuck on fuel

functions.type: open library for motor control, logging and paths

facts.text: All motors use torque FOC control
Its trajectory generator can make paths on the fly; a background script nudges path points to save time
A script reads match logs for time to score, time to align and flywheel energy lost
One button runs an automated pit check of drive, hood, pivot and shooter
The pit check runs in test mode: commands drive each subsystem in turn, and a controller input moves to the next

decisions.because: it raises fuel per second, so the robot scores larger loads and is less limited by fuel starvation
the team trusts software tuning to handle velocity spikes and still spins up in about 0.4 s
decisions.instead_of: a separate flywheel and four or more motors

decisions.because: when a mass of fuel comes in, it only has to get into the hopper, not be controlled piece by piece
the linear intake shredded teeth, took hopper space when deployed and left the team unhappy with its robustness at the first event; the pivot follows one that 10118 showed the team there

decisions.choice: Hopper that fits under the trench
decisions.because: it lets the robot cross the field when the bump is defended

decisions.choice: Stationary hopper panels on the bumpers
decisions.because: they add storage, and bumper mounting hardware does not count toward the weight limit
the powered one helped less than expected; a static one saves weight and leaves current for other subsystems
they reduce weight and complexity and are more compact
decisions.instead_of: a telescoping climber, prototyped early but never competed with

decisions.choice: Electrical panel flipped right side up
decisions.because: it protects the electronics from the bump and from fuel under the robot
